summary: Mid-contract check-in focused on Stellarus' renewal conversation: capacity tiering, APAC region activation, and contract extension options. Redwood presented tiered pricing with burst options; SE reviewed latency/throughput tradeoffs and KV cache behavior. Customer asked for SOC2/KMS confirmation and trial validation criteria. Agreed next steps: send benchmarks, run pilot, and align legal questions.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-19 16:00 UTC — Duration 58 minutes
Attendees noted above. Recording started.

[00:00] Alicia Park: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is Alicia from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, joined by Rohan our SE and Tom who's supporting success. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Marta Alvarez: Hi Alicia, doing well, thanks. We have Kenji and Priya on — just a quick note, Priya will chime on anything legal/compliance.
[00:12] Kenji Sato: Morning, thanks.
[00:15] Priya Desai: Hello.
[00:20] Alicia Park: Great. Goal for today — walk through renewal options and the APAC onramp plan, align on capacity tiers and pilot validation. Rohan will go through the perf tradeoffs.
[00:30] Rohan Mehta: Yep, I'll jump into the runtime and caching stuff, and how the dedicated pools look. Quick question before we start — Marta, are you expecting to move full traffic to APAC or phase it?
[00:38] Marta Alvarez: Phase. We want a small active routing to APAC for inference-heavy endpoints first — mainly inference for our assistant product. We're trying to keep the training infra in US, inference near users in APAC.
[00:47] Alicia Park: Makes sense. From the pricing side we recommended the tiered approach — base committed TPU/GPU hours for US plus a smaller reserve for APAC, and burst capacity on top.
[00:56] Kenji Sato: When you say burst capacity — is that the same as your Dedicated burst pool or is it a hosted fallback? I get confused with the different modes.
[01:04] Rohan Mehta: Good question. For Stellarus' profile, burst can be served from the same Dedicated pool if you enable the burst nodes — they spin up in the same region. Fallback to Hosted is also possible but we'd route to a compatible model variant with a slightly different quantization profile. There's a latency delta.
[01:20] Marta Alvarez: How big is the latency delta if you route to hosted? We need 99th percentile under 220ms for our APAC endpoint.
[01:28] Rohan Mehta: In our APAC benchmarks, fallback to hosted added around 60–120ms to token streaming depending on model size and seq length. For short prompts it's smaller, for longer streaming responses it can be more noticeable because of batching behaviors and KV cache warmup.
[01:45] Alicia Park: We'll send the APAC bucketed latencies in a spreadsheet after this call. That will include baseline Dedicated numbers and hosted-fallback numbers during peak.
[01:52] Kenji Sato: Perfect — we'll need the 99p numbers. Also can you call out the node counts you used?
[01:58] Rohan Mehta: Yes, we'll attach the suggested node counts and a quick config for KV cache TTL and prefix caching. One note — our transcription sometimes writes K V cash, so apologies for the transcript.
[02:08] (laughter)
[02:12] Marta Alvarez: No worries.
[02:15] Priya Desai: On compliance, can you confirm whether audit logs include token-level anonymized payloads or just meta? We need to confirm data residency for some PHI-ish flows.
[02:25] Alicia Park: Short answer: logs contain metadata and hashed identifiers by default. For Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) customers can choose to ship logs to their own S3 / SIEM and enable full audit retention. We do pseudonymization options as well. We'll send the SOC 2 / KMS & audit doc links.
[02:40] Priya Desai: Ok, good. Also need to know encryption at rest keys — do you support customer-managed KMS in your Private offering?
[02:48] Rohan Mehta: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS, including external HSMs in some setups. For Hosted we manage keys; for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own keys and we log key usage. We'll include the KMS integration matrix.
[03:02] Kenji Sato: When you do Dedicated in APAC — is the control plane still out of region? Latency to control plane matters because some re-allocs are control-plane driven.
[03:10] Rohan Mehta: Control plane remains in the central region for now but we have regional proxies to reduce control-plane latencies. For the operations that affect runtime, we do most actions asynchronously so there's not a synchronous dependency that impacts the 99p inference. We'll go into more detail in the doc.
[03:25] Alicia Park: Ok, shifting to the renewal structure — we proposed a 12-month extension with a three-tier capacity ladder: Small (base), Medium (base + burst), Large (higher base + committed burst). Each tier has an associated discount and priority for provisioning during supply constraints.
[03:39] Marta Alvarez: Our finance prefers the Medium; but we want to understand the economics if we commit to Medium in US and base in APAC versus committing to Medium across both.
[03:48] Alicia Park: Right. There's a non-linear step in unit cost when committing at global scale because we can optimize cross-region placement of multi-tenant nodes; cost per token drops. I'll attach a modeling sheet that shows per-token delta at 10M, 50M, 250M tokens/month.
[04:04] Kenji Sato: Could we get a scenario that keeps US base at Medium and APAC at a small pilot for three months with a fast uplift trigger if latency targets are met?
[04:13] Tom Anders: We can bake that into the contract as a staged uplift clause — e.g., upgrade APAC to Medium within 30 days of reaching 99p < 220ms for two consecutive weeks during the pilot. Legal will need that text.
[04:26] Priya Desai: Yes, we'll require a clear SLA clause and an exit clause if numbers are not met. Also want clarity about data deletion windows for transient logs.
[04:34] Alicia Park: Understood. We'll draft sample SLA language and the staged uplift clause.
[04:38] [06:10] (rough jump — speaker overlap, ambient typing)
[06:15] Rohan Mehta: I want to highlight a technical tradeoff: turning on heavy batching improves throughput and lowers tokens/sec cost but increases tail latency. For user-facing assistant endpoints with strict 99p latency constraints we recommend continuous small-batch mode + prefix caching. That preserves latency while still giving cost benefits.
[06:32] Marta Alvarez: When you say prefix caching, is that the Redwood prefix cache or something we host ourselves?
[06:37] Rohan Mehta: It's Redwood-managed KV cache for model keys. For Private deployments we can provide a customer-hosted cache option. There are limits to cache size per node; we'll propose configuration.
[06:48] Kenji Sato: Any special tuning for long-context conversations? We have history windows of 8–12k tokens for some flows.
[06:55] Rohan Mehta: For that profile we use streaming KV eviction and compressed kv formats. There's also quantization-friendly execution paths. We'll share recommended quantization profiles and expected perf lift.
[07:08] Marta Alvarez: Can you also include guidance for model pinning and rollbacks? We don't want a noisy rollout to affect latency.
[07:14] Rohan Mehta: Absolutely. Our rollout tool supports canary percentages, automatic rollback on throughput regressions, and a fallback policy to a previous model variant. We'll include the runbook.
[07:22] Alicia Park: Quick commercial question — if we include a three-month APAC pilot with a performance gate, does Redwood consider prorated credits if the gate fails?
[07:30] Tom Anders: We typically include operational credits or extended trial windows; credits are negotiated per-deal. We'll propose a credit structure in the pricing addendum.
[07:38] Priya Desai: Would like that in writing.
[07:40] Alicia Park: We'll include it.
[07:42] [15:02] (mid-discussion; Rohan screens through perf slides; ambient comments)
[15:15] Marta Alvarez: I have one more question — latency SLA for model variants. For the assistant we need consistent latency across a family of models (medium and small variants) because we route different users.
[15:25] Rohan Mehta: The runtime profiles per variant differ; we'll show expected 50/95/99p for each variant. If you require strict parity we recommend reserving capacity for the larger variant and using auto-scaling to bring up the small ones as needed.
[15:40] Kenji Sato: Ok. Regarding connectivity — do you support private link/VPC endpoints for the APAC region?
[15:47] Alicia Park: Yes, Private deployments support VPC peering and PrivateLink for hosted endpoints. We'll attach the network topology doc for APAC.
[15:55] Priya Desai: Also confirm export controls and restricted data handling — some of our customers in Health require stricter handling.
[16:03] Alicia Park: We'll include the compliance matrix. For PHI flows we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict KMS and logging to your SIEM.
[16:12] Marta Alvarez: On the pilot validation — what metrics should we capture? We propose 99p latency, avg tokens/sec, error rate, percent routed to fallback, and cost per 1k tokens. Anything else?
[16:23] Rohan Mehta: That's good. Add cold start percent and KV cache hit rate. We'll instrument those via the console and share dashboards.
[16:31] Kenji Sato: Can you create a temporary dashboard for us during the trial?
[16:35] Tom Anders: Yes, we'll provision a read-only dashboard and give you token-level slices for the pilot.
[16:41] [26:00] (product/ops tangents)
[26:10] Marta Alvarez: Thinking out loud — if we commit to the Medium tier and see 30% more traffic, what is the lead time for provisioning extra nodes in APAC? We need rapid scaling.
[26:20] Rohan Mehta: With burst nodes enabled, the typical spin-up is 8–12 minutes to spin and warm a node, depending on model size. To get that down we recommend keeping a small reserve and using prefix caching primed for expected top prompts.
[26:33] Kenji Sato: Noted.
[26:36] Priya Desai: Quick legal: is the staged uplift clause compatible with your standard amendment flow or do we need a separate SOW?
[26:43] Alicia Park: We can do a contract addendum that includes staged uplift language and the performance gate. We'll draft sample wording and share.
[26:50] Priya Desai: Great.
[26:54] [36:20] (wrap-up discussion and recaps)
[36:30] Alicia Park: To recap — action items: we'll send APAC benchmarks + node counts, a draft staged-uplift clause and pricing addendum with credit structure. Rohan will propose pilot config and dashboards. Stellarus will share the 7-day token trace and legal requirements.
[36:48] Marta Alvarez: That's accurate. I think the staged approach is right. If the pilot hits the gate we'll accelerate.
[36:56] Kenji Sato: We'll try to get the traces to you by Tuesday.
[36:59] Priya Desai: I'll follow up with legal questions; expect 1–2 items.
[37:04] Tom Anders: We'll tentatively schedule a pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-02 — I'll send a Doodle.
[37:11] Alicia Park: Thanks everyone — we'll share the docs. Any last questions?
[37:15] (brief silence)
[37:17] Marta Alvarez: No, that's it. Thanks.
[37:20] Alicia Park: Awesome. Talk soon. Bye.
[37:23] (recording stopped)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K V cash). References to shared artifacts: APAC-performance.xlsx (will be attached), staged-uplift-sample.docx, pilot-dashboard-readonly link.

End of file.
